utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-R77.2, the Prosecutor versus Jelena Rasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances, please. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to my colleagues in the courtroom. Paul Rogers appearing on behalf of the Prosecution, together with my learned friend Mr. Kyle Wood and our Case Manager today, Ms. Jasmina Bosnjakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For Ms. Rasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Mira Tapuskovic. I'm the attorney-at-law from Belgrade. Today I'm going to represent as duty counsel Jelena Rasic during Initial Appearance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mrs. Rasic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe the microphone wasn't on. I'm going to ask you repeat so that this is on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had trouble finding the channel with Serbian interpretation, but now it's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please tell me if you have any other problem, and don't hesitate to let me know about it if you do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Mrs. Jelena Rasic's Initial Appearance according to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the ICTY. The indictment against Mrs. Rasic has been examined and confirmed by a Judge of this Tribunal on the 26th of August, 2010. This case has been assigned to a Trial Chamber on the 16th of September, 2010, and since the Judges sitting on this Chamber were unable to attend today, I am sitting today as a Duty Judge pursuant to Rule 28 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Mrs. Rasic was transferred to the Tribunal on the 20th of September, 2010. Mrs. Rasic, could you stand up, please, and answer the following questions. Is your microphone on?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you give me your first name and last name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jelena Rasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 19th of April, 1983, in Sibenik, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Rasic, pursuant to the Statute and the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, you are entitled to remain silent throughout the entire proceedings. A duty counsel has been assigned to assist you during this hearing, Mrs. Tapuskovic. Are you satisfied with the counsel that has been assigned?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you had the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did your counsel explain to you what was contained in the indictment and the counts described therein against you? I think you need to repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She did, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Rasic, do you have any health problems or any other problems relating to your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may sit down, Mrs. Rasic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I noted that the indictment had been filed confidentially. Can this indictment be made public? Is anything standing in the way of lifting the confidentiality of this indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. There's -- there's nothing standing in the way of removing the confidentiality on this indictment. Indeed, it should be made public. Your Honour will note the -- within it the references to X and Y. My learned friend and her client know who those individuals are. There's no need for them to be named or mentioned in public for reasons which Your Honour and my learned friends are aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And these have already been identified for the purposes of the Tribunal. Mrs. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not oppose the lifting of confidentiality in respect of the indictment. The identity of the witnesses stated in the indictment will be kept confidential by both myself and my client. So I do agree that the confidentiality status be lifted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So if there are no objections, I order the lifting of the confidentiality status of the indictment. The accused is entitled to a reading out of the indictment in a language she understands. You can, however, waive this right and accept that a summary of the indictment be read out. Ms. Tapuskovic, does your client wish to have the indictment read out in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since in the course of the two yesterday's visits we went through the indictment twice, my client agrees that the indictment need not be read out in its entirety but only in summary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall therefore have a reading of the summary of the indictment. Madam Registrar, do you have a summary of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar will read out the summary of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor versus Rasic, summary of the indictment. The indictment alleges that at all material times, Mrs. Rasic was acting as a member of the Milan Lukic Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the Registrar please read out slowly for the benefit of the interpreters. The interpreters do not have the text of the summary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I will. Thank you. Count 1 of the indictment alleges that on -- on or about 18th October 2008, Mrs. Rasic met Zuhdija Tabakovic in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and showed Mr. Tabakovic a pre-prepared witness statement for use in the Lukic and Lukic case. Mrs. Rasic asked Mr. Tabakovic if he would sign the statement in exchange for 1.000 euros. Mrs. Rasic promised Mr. Tabakovic more money if he testified in accordance with the statement on behalf of Milan Lukic. On 20th October 2008, Mrs. Rasic met with Mr. Tabakovic who signed multiple copies of the statement. The statement was false, as Mr. Tabakovic had no knowledge of the events described in the statement. Mrs. Rasic gave Mr. Tabakovic 1.000 euros. Count 2 of the indictment alleges that on 18th October 2008, Mrs. Rasic showed Mr. Tabakovic two other pre-prepared statements for use in the Lukic and Lukic case. Mrs. Rasic offered Mr. Tabakovic a reward to find other men born in Visegrad to sign these false statements. Mr. Tabakovic agreed to find other men to sign -- to sign the statements. Counts 3 and 4 of the indictment allege that on a date between 17th and 24th October 2008, Mr. Tabakovic met with Mr. X and Mr. Y and asked each man whether he would be willing to -- to sign a statement in exchange for payment of 1.000 euros. Both agreed to sign a statement knowing that he would be providing a false statement. On 23rd October 2008, Mr. Tabakovic introduced Mr. X and Mr. Y to it Mr. -- to Mrs. Rasic. Mr. X and Mr. Y signed the statements and each received 1.000 euros. Count 5 of the indictment alleges that between 23rd October and 6 December 2008, Mrs. Rasic returned to Sarajevo with revised versions of the false statements signed by Mr. Tabakovic, Mr. X and Mr. Y.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mrs. Rasic gave Mr. Tabakovic three unsigned revised statements and asked him to sign his own statement and to ask Mr. X and Mr. Y to sign theirs. Each statement was false. All three statements, dated 5 December 2008, were signed and returned to Mrs. Rasic. On 20th January 2009, lead counsel for Milan Lukic gave copies of the signed 5th December 2008 statements to the Prosecution. As a result of the allegations contained in the indictment, Mrs. Rasic is charged with five counts of contempt of the Tribunal punishable under this Tribunal's inherent powers and Rule 77(A) of the Rules for knowingly and wilfully interfering with the administration of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. We shall now move on to the arguments relating to the counts of the indictment. Pursuant to Rule 62(A)(iii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, you may choose to plead guilty or not guilty as regards each count of the indictment. You may do so right now, or you may do so within 30 days as of today. If you do not plead either way today or during an appearance at a later stage, the Trial Chamber will note on your behalf that this amounts to a plea of not guilty. Ms. Tapuskovic, does your client wish to plead today or at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, she would like to plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mrs. Rasic, could you stand up, please. Can you tell us what you are pleading. Are you pleading guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty on all -- all the counts of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, can you note that Mrs. Rasic has pleaded not guilty on each count of the indictment. I must now remind the Prosecutor that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, he must disclose to the Defence within 30 days in a language that the accused understands a copy of all the annexes of the indictment when this has been confirmed, as well as all the prior statements of the accused's that have been received. I would also like to remind the Defence that once it has received all these documents, it will have 30 days to file its preliminary motions. The Trial Chamber which is seized of this case will set the date for our next hearing, and you will be advised in due course. Are there any questions which either party wishes to raise before we adjourn for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the only matter that I would just raise is I think that the -- under the Rules the time limit relating to the provision of -- oh, yes. The filing of preliminary motions - I'm sorry - doesn't run until permanent counsel has been assigned to Ms. Rasic under Rule 72(A)(iv), and it's 10 days, not 30 days, because under Rule 77 the time limits were truncated for contempt cases, and so the 30-day time limits in many of the aspects of the Rules have been replaced with a 10-day time limit. But so far as the provision of materials to the Defence is concerned, we have already provided most of it. There is a small amount that -- that will be forthcoming within the next ten days. So all of that will be complied with in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Rasic is entitled to choose a permanent counsel or to represent herself, and she has 30 days in which to do this. In addition, the deadline I mentioned only runs once a permanent counsel has been assigned. Mrs. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would only like to confirm what my learned friend Mr. Rogers stated. Yesterday in my contacts with the Prosecution, I received most of the supporting material accompanying the indictment, and we agreed that the remainder would be disclosed to me or, rather, to another Defence counsel should Ms. Rasic choose another one within the -- in the course of the next couple of days, and we agreed that Ms. Rasic would receive her copy of the supporting material now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Are there any further questions? If there are no further questions, the court stands adjourned for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: at 9.22 a.m.
